subject: EU-only processing and SCCs — technical + contractual playbook request
messages:
From: Anna Kovács <anna.kovacs@medisyshealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: LegalOps <legalops@medisyshealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T08:12:00Z
Subject: EU-only processing + SCCs — initial questions

Hi Sergio,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our procurement and legal teams are running through the vendor checklist and we have a couple of high-priority questions before we move to procurement: 

1) Can you confirm you can commit to EU-only processing for MediSys customer data (i.e., ingress, processing, and short-term KV caches residing in EU regions only)?
2) Do you accept EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) as the transfer mechanism? If so, can we get a mapping table showing sub-processor locations and data flows mapped to SCCs clauses?
3) Retention/deletion: how do you handle deletion requests and backups (time-to-delete, proof-of-deletion/evidence)?
4) Are there any components (telemetry, monitoring, auth) that still talk to non-EU endpoints?

Procurement would like answers and any supporting artifacts (architecture diagram, SCCs mapping, DPA annex) by next Wednesday so we can hit our quarter close. I'm attaching our (short) security questionnaire for reference.

Appreciate a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Anna Kovács
Head of Procurement
MediSys Health
[Attachment: MediSys_Security_Questionnaire.pdf]

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Anna Kovács <anna.kovacs@medisyshealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T12:40:00Z
Subject: Re: EU-only processing + SCCs — initial questions

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers here and we'll follow up with artifacts (and a technical runbook) shortly: 

- EU-only processing: Yes — we offer region pinning and can keep customer workspaces + runtime in EU regions (Frankfurt/Paris/Amsterdam). Short-lived KV caches used for generation are retained only in-region and we can disable any cross-region replication for your tenant.
- SCCs: We accept SCCs and can sign an amendment. We maintain a sub-processor list and will provide a clause-by-clause mapping.
- Retention/deletion: We support immediate customer-initiated deletion via the Console/API; primary data removal is within 24 hours, snapshots/backups are purged within 30 days by default (we can negotiate shorter windows). We provide an exportable proof-of-deletion record (audit log + job ID).
- Telemetry/endpoints: Most observability hooks are region-local; a small set of telemetry aggregation endpoints are EU-hosted for dedicated/private customers. For hosted customers we can provide an option to reduce telemetry to EU-only endpoints.

I've looped in Neha (security) and Laura (legal) to prepare the SCCs mapping and DPA annex. I'll attach our architecture diagram now so your engineers have something to review.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call tomorrow (Apr 19) 09:00 CEST to walk the team through the architecture + SCCs mapping. Does that work?

Cheers,
Sergio
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-eu-processing-architecture.png]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Anna Kovács <anna.kovacs@medisyshealth.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: EU-only processing + SCCs — technical details

Hi Anna and team,

Following up from the architecture call — here are the technical details we discussed and the specific artifacts we're attaching. I'll keep this focused so your engineers can validate quickly.

1) Data residency and runtime
- Control plane: customer metadata and account control plane (control-plane APIs) are located in EU for in-region customers; control-plane traffic is TLS-only and logged.
- Serving runtime: model inference pods and KV caches run in EU zones only for a pinned tenant. KV caches are ephemeral (TTL default 30s-60s depending on workload) and stored in memory/local SSD within the region.

2) SCCs mapping
- Attached: SCCs_Mapping_Table.xlsx — maps SCC clauses to our subprocessors/services and EU/non-EU data flows. Note: subprocessors with non-EU admin domains only have access to metadata (billing/job telemetry) which can be excluded via config.

3) Retention & deletion
- Primary data deletion: immediate job that marks data for removal and triggers async purge; completion job emits audit entry with job ID and timestamp.
- Backups & snapshots: default 30-day retention; configurable down to 7 days for enterprise contracts.
- Proof-of-deletion: we provide audit log export + manifest and signed attestation for enterprise customers upon request.

4) Telemetry/third-party endpoints
- We can enforce EU-only telemetry collectors for your tenant. Any external monitoring integration (PagerDuty, Sentry) must be configured to EU endpoints on your side.

Attachments included: SCCs_Mapping_Table.xlsx (mapping), runbook excerpt (pasted below).

Runbook excerpt:
- Step 1: Tenant pin request (Console -> Support ticket) -> confirm region and disable cross-region replication.
- Step 2: Validation job (infra) -> confirm no active tokens/pipelines in non-EU region.
- Step 3: DPA & SCCs sign-off -> legal signature -> schedule go-live.

If you want, we can shorten the backup window to 14 days in the amendment; let me know.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SCCs_Mapping_Table.xlsx]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Anna Kovács <anna.kovacs@medisyshealth.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T10:15:00Z
Subject: Re: EU-only processing + SCCs — contractual path

Hi Anna — thanks for the detailed questions and thanks Neha for the mapping. From a legal path perspective, here's what we suggest so we can get you to procurement sign-off quickly: 

1) DPA amendment: we will execute a short DPA amendment that incorporates the EU SCCs (2021 modular clauses) and an Annex listing subprocessors and the EU-only routing commitment. I've attached a draft (redwood-dpa-annex-sccs_v1.pdf) and a redline of the amendment that highlights the EU-only processing clause.
2) Backup window: we'll offer 14 days backup retention in the DPA for MediSys; that will be stated expressly in Section 4.1 of the Annex.
3) Proof-of-deletion: we will include a standard deletion attestation template and an operational SLA to provide proof within 5 business days of request.
4) Signature flow: we prefer DocuSign for speed; propose Redwood signs first, then MediSys countersigns. I've prepared the redlined amendment (redlined_amendment_v2.pdf).

Next actions for us: Sergio, can you confirm the exact legal recipient/email for the DocuSign envelope? Anna, please confirm whether MediSys requires any additional contractual language about in-region key management (we currently provide KMS integrations and can offer EU KMS options).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-dpa-annex-sccs_v1.pdf]
[Attachment: redlined_amendment_v2.pdf]

From: Anna Kovács <anna.kovacs@medisyshealth.com>

Cc: LegalOps <legalops@medisyshealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: EU-only processing + SCCs — contractual path

Hi all,

This is very helpful — thanks for the fast turnaround. Procurement/legal reviewed the mapping and the draft DPA annex and we are generally comfortable with the approach. A couple quick items: 

- Please send the DocuSign envelope to legalops@medisyshealth.com (Legal Ops will countersign).
- Could you also provide a final architecture diagram that highlights EU-only datapaths (PNG or PDF) so our engineering team can confirm there are no non-EU hops?
- We accept the 14-day backup window and the 5-business-day deletion attestation SLA.

Target: we'd like to have the amendment signed by Apr 27 so procurement can release the PO by Apr 30. If you can send the DocuSign link today that would be ideal. I've attached our internal requirements doc for transparency.

Thanks,
Anna
Head of Procurement
MediSys Health
